response.title: how long will a solar generator run
response.answer:
A solar generator can run anywhere from a few hours to several days, depending on its battery capacity, how much electricity your devices use, and whether solar panels are recharging it.

Unlike a gas generator, a solar generator stores electricity in a battery and can be recharged by sunlight.

Estimated runtime by battery size

Assuming the battery starts fully charged, with no solar recharging:

These estimates assume 85% usable energy after conversion losses.

What if you have solar panels?

With sufficient solar panels and sunlight, a solar generator can potentially run indefinitely, provided that daily solar energy production meets or exceeds your daily electricity consumption.

For example, a 2,000Wh solar generator with 400W of solar panels might generate roughly 1,200–1,600Wh per sunny day, depending on conditions.

markup:
A **solar generator can run anywhere from a few hours to several days**, depending on its battery capacity, how much electricity your devices use, and whether solar panels are recharging it.

Unlike a gas generator, a solar generator stores electricity in a battery and can be recharged by sunlight.

## Estimated runtime by battery size

Assuming the battery starts fully charged, with no solar recharging:

| Battery capacity | 100W device | 500W device | 1,000W device |
|---|---|---|---|
| 500Wh | 4.3 hours | 0.85 hours | 0.43 hours |
| 1,000Wh | 8.5 hours | 1.7 hours | 0.85 hours |
| 2,000Wh | 17 hours | 3.4 hours | 1.7 hours |
| 5,000Wh | 42.5 hours | 8.5 hours | 4.25 hours |

These estimates assume 85% usable energy after conversion losses.

## What if you have solar panels?

With sufficient solar panels and sunlight, a solar generator can potentially run **indefinitely**, provided that daily solar energy production meets or exceeds your daily electricity consumption.

For example, a 2,000Wh solar generator with 400W of solar panels might generate roughly 1,200–1,600Wh per sunny day, depending on conditions.

## Calculate your runtime

{@body const [battery,setBattery] = DIL.useState("2000")}
{@body const [watts,setWatts] = DIL.useState("100")}
{@body const runtime = Number(battery)*0.85/Number(watts)}

      <radio value="500">500Wh</radio>
      <radio value="1000">1,000Wh</radio>
      <radio value="2000">2,000Wh</radio>
      <radio value="5000">5,000Wh</radio>
    </radio-group>
  </box>
  <box gap={1}>
    <label>Power consumption</label>
    <radio-group direction="col" value={watts} onChange={setWatts}>
      <radio value="50">50W — small fan / electronics</radio>
      <radio value="100">100W — TV / small appliance</radio>
      <radio value="500">500W — multiple appliances</radio>
      <radio value="1000">1,000W — high-power appliance</radio>
    </radio-group>
  </box>
  <box background="surface-secondary" padding={3} radius="lg" gap={1}>
    <text color="secondary" weight="medium" size="xs">Estimated runtime without sunlight</text>
    <title size="2xl" color="default" tabularNums>{runtime >= 24 ? `${(runtime/24).toFixed(1)} days` : `${runtime.toFixed(1)} hours`}</title>
    <caption>Assumes constant power consumption and 85% usable battery energy.</caption>
  </box>
</box>
